nodes.label: AWS EC2 host ip-172-31-45-137 (Ubuntu)
nodes.rationale: 17 pending package updates, 6 of them security, plus a pending system restart at the time of capture.

nodes.label: Duplicate inventory_rooms rows created per CSV row
nodes.norm_label: duplicate inventory_rooms rows created per csv row
nodes.rationale: Second defect visible in the same query log: every CSV row runs `select * from inventory_rooms where (branch_id = 1 and code = 'IT-OFFICE') and deleted_at is null limit 1` and then still inserts a new 'IT OFFICE' room (ids 1..11 within one import). The firstOrCreate lookup never sees the row it just wrote — most likely because the write happens inside an uncommitted/rolled-back import transaction or the lookup runs on a stale/different connection. Result: 11 identical IT-OFFICE rooms and 11 activity_log 'created' entries for one office.

nodes.label: Duplicate login_sessions insert on a single request
nodes.norm_label: duplicate login_sessions insert on a single request
nodes.rationale: The same login_sessions row for user 410 is inserted twice at 13:10:15 on one POST /livewire/update, suggesting the login-tracking listener is registered twice or fires on both Login and Authenticated events.

nodes.label: QueryException: Unknown column 'tenstrings_office_name' on inventory_items insert
nodes.norm_label: queryexception: unknown column 'tenstrings_office_name' on inventory_items insert
nodes.rationale: SQLSTATE[42S22] 1054 raised on portal.tenstrings.org (PHP 8.3.30, Laravel 12.53.0) during Filament import 12 of an inventory CSV. The CSV column 'TENSTRINGS OFFICE NAME' was mapped to a model attribute 'tenstrings_office_name' that has no matching column on inventory_items, so Eloquent put the helper value straight into the INSERT. Fix direction: strip CSV-only helper fields before save (resolve them into branch_id/inventory_room_id and the notes string instead).

nodes.label: /payments mobile endpoints
nodes.rationale: Read-only history, fee-status and signed receipt URLs; initiating a payment from mobile is a 501 stub pending a WebView or deep-linking strategy.

nodes.label: DocumentService::generateReceiptPdf
nodes.rationale: Receipt PDFs are generated with Barryvdh\DomPDF from the pdf.receipt view, passing the Payment with student and invoice relations loaded.

nodes.label: PaymentService
nodes.rationale: handleWebhook() is the single reconciliation point: it sets status/payment_status, amount_paid, processed_at, receipt_number and metadata.receipt_path, then cascades into StudentCourseFee, Student balances and PaymentAdvice. reconcileTgiPayPayment() verifies TGIPAY status out-of-band.

nodes.label: Paystack webhook signature verification
nodes.rationale: hash_hmac('sha512', rawPayload, webhookSecret) compared with hash_equals against the x-paystack-signature header.

nodes.label: TgiPayGateway
nodes.rationale: Server-to-server flow authenticated with an integration-key header instead of a bearer token or signature hash; amounts are sent as plain naira floats and there is no HMAC signature verification.

nodes.label: Automated WhatsApp fee reminders
nodes.rationale: Built on the unofficial Evolution API specifically to bypass Meta's official API constraints - no message templates and no per-message fees. MD approved two automated messages per week to debtors after the due date.

nodes.label: 200 OK on failed signature
nodes.rationale: The controller deliberately returns 200 even when signature validation fails, to stop the gateway retrying endlessly.

nodes.label: Webhook CSRF exclusion
nodes.rationale: Done with ->withoutMiddleware([VerifyCsrfToken::class]) directly on the route in routes/web.php rather than through the VerifyCsrfToken exceptions array.

nodes.label: Paystack kobo amount conversion
nodes.rationale: Paystack amounts must be multiplied by 100 when sending and divided by 100 when receiving, while TGIPAY uses actual naira floats - mixing the two silently produces 100x errors.

nodes.label: Redundant payment status tracking
nodes.rationale: payments carries both the legacy payment_status (paid/partial/pending) and the modern status (pending/processing/success/failed); both must be written during reconciliation to avoid breaking legacy code.

nodes.label: cache_locks queue overlap lock for ImportCsv
nodes.norm_label: cache_locks queue overlap lock for importcsv
nodes.rationale: Lock key 'laravel-queue-overlap:Filament\Actions\Imports\Jobs\ImportCsv:import12' shows the import job runs under WithoutOverlapping per import id.

nodes.label: failed_import_rows table
nodes.rationale: Rows are written here even when validation_error is NULL, so the table is also recording successfully-parsed rows — a symptom worth checking alongside the import crash.

nodes.label: Filament\Actions\Imports\Jobs\ImportCsv
nodes.rationale: Runs the row insert inside DB::transaction (ManagesTransactions frame), which is why a mid-import crash can roll back rooms created earlier in the same batch.

nodes.label: POST /livewire/update (default.livewire.update)
nodes.rationale: The import was triggered synchronously from the Livewire update round-trip on /inventory/inventory-items, so the queued ImportCsv exception surfaced as a 500 in the admin UI.

nodes.label: FileUpload::make('image') on room form
nodes.rationale: Lets category/room images be uploaded and edited in place, which is what makes the collapsed room headers and the card grid readable.

nodes.label: InventoryTransfer model and migration
nodes.rationale: Tracks item_id, destination (event or campus name), type and date so equipment leaving a room has an auditable trail.

nodes.label: Action::make('transfer') modal
nodes.rationale: A table action collects destination, type and date, then writes the InventoryTransfer row and updates the item's status in one submission, so the log and the item state cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: Payment knowledge extraction task (read-only agent brief)
nodes.norm_label: payment knowledge extraction task (read-only agent brief)
nodes.rationale: Rather than copying the portal's payment code into a new project, a senior-dev agent reads the live implementation and writes a faithful knowledge document a second agent can build from — keeping the source project untouched while transferring the hard-won gateway details.

nodes.label: Paystack server-side verification
nodes.rationale: Inline-JS or redirect, the backend must re-verify the reference against Paystack's verify endpoint with the secret token before updating the DB — the frontend callback alone is not trusted.

nodes.label: Post-payment success redirect and PDF generation
nodes.norm_label: post-payment success redirect and pdf generation

nodes.label: TGI Titan payment gateway
nodes.rationale: Redirect-style gateway: initiation POST with signed fields, customer redirect to a hosted page, then a webhook callback that must be signature-verified before the payment record is marked paid.

nodes.label: Titan HMAC/signature construction
nodes.rationale: What is hashed, with which key, and in what field order is the single most error-prone part of the integration, so the knowledge doc must capture it verbatim.

nodes.label: Asset tag scheme TS-<office>-<sequence>
nodes.rationale: Tags such as TS-IT-000..TS-IT-010 and TS-AJA-AUD-0001 are probed with a per-tag `select exists(... where asset_tag = ?)` before each insert, so uniqueness is enforced by lookup rather than a DB constraint.

nodes.label: 4-column contentGrid item layout
nodes.rationale: ->contentGrid(['md' => 2, 'xl' => 4]) turns the item table into a card grid so photos are scannable at a glance instead of buried in table rows.

nodes.label: PAYMENT_KNOWLEDGE.md deliverable
nodes.rationale: Seven fixed sections (Titan flow, Paystack flow, database, post-payment, routes, config keys, lessons/gotchas); every snippet must be copied from real code, missing files flagged as NOT FOUND, and all credentials replaced with dummy placeholders.

nodes.label: Validation error: 'The iTEM field is required.'
nodes.norm_label: validation error: 'the item field is required.'
nodes.rationale: Blank CSV rows fail with an awkwardly cased attribute label ('iTEM'), showing the importer derives validation labels from raw uppercase CSV headers instead of declared column labels.

nodes.label: Webhook CSRF exclusion and retry gotchas
nodes.norm_label: webhook csrf exclusion and retry gotchas
nodes.rationale: Gateway callbacks are external POSTs with no session, so they must be excluded from CSRF middleware; retry logic and other non-obvious edge cases are the things a fresh agent reimplementing the flow is most likely to get wrong.

nodes.label: Dummy-credential rule for extracted config keys
nodes.norm_label: dummy-credential rule for extracted config keys
nodes.rationale: Only payment-related keys are lifted from .env.example and every value is replaced with a placeholder (TITAN_SECRET=your_titan_secret_here) so a shared knowledge doc never carries live secrets.

nodes.label: Read-only extraction constraint
nodes.rationale: DO NOT build anything, DO NOT modify any files — the production school portal must not be destabilised by a documentation pass.

nodes.label: CSV helper fields leaking into Eloquent insert
nodes.norm_label: csv helper fields leaking into eloquent insert
nodes.rationale: An importer that keeps spreadsheet-only columns (office name, item code, raw item text) on the model record will crash at INSERT time with a column-not-found error. Helper columns must be consumed during resolution and then unset, never persisted.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive duplicate item guard (LOWER(name) per room)
nodes.norm_label: case-insensitive duplicate item guard (lower(name) per room)
nodes.rationale: Before inserting, the importer checks `exists(... branch_id = ? and inventory_room_id = ? and LOWER(name) = ? and deleted_at is null)` so re-running a CSV does not duplicate items; the guard is scoped per branch and room and ignores soft-deleted rows.

nodes.label: No Filament core Blade view overrides
nodes.norm_label: no filament core blade view overrides
nodes.rationale: Published core views drift from upstream and break on Filament upgrades, so the grid and grouping must come from the PHP Table Builder API alone; unavoidable CSS goes through FilamentView::registerRenderHook() scoped to ListInventoryItems::class so it cannot leak into other pages.

nodes.label: Collapsible grouping by room, collapsed by default
nodes.norm_label: collapsible grouping by room, collapsed by default
nodes.rationale: Group::make('room.name')->collapsible() with everything collapsed means the first screen is just a list of room names; expanding one reveals its items in the 4-column grid, keeping a large inventory navigable.

nodes.label: ScopedToBranch trait (global branch scope)
nodes.rationale: A global Eloquent scope constrains every query to the user's branch_id unless they hold inventory.view_all_branches, so scoping cannot be forgotten at the call site.

nodes.label: Role access matrix feature test
nodes.rationale: A real feature test asserting inventory_officer gets 403 on /admin and on the student and payment resources, because this is the requirement most likely to silently regress.

nodes.label: Asset tag generation (TS-{BRANCH}-{CAT}-{0001})
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated in an InventoryItem observer when left blank, sequenced per branch + category inside a DB transaction with lockForUpdate() on the counter row so two officers saving at once cannot collide; manual override is allowed because some assets arrive with existing organisational tags.

nodes.label: Denormalised branch_id on items
nodes.rationale: branch_id is kept on the item even though the room implies it, because it makes branch scoping and reporting cheap and survives a room being deleted; an observer re-syncs it whenever inventory_room_id changes.

nodes.label: inventory_checkout_items table
nodes.rationale: Each line carries condition_out/condition_in reusing the existing item condition values rather than inventing new ones, plus returned_quantity, received_by and a return_status of returned_ok / returned_damaged / missing.

nodes.label: InventoryCheckoutService
nodes.rationale: checkout() and return() live in a service called by the Filament actions so the mobile API can reuse the same logic later.

nodes.label: inventory_checkouts table
nodes.rationale: Modelled as an event-level checkout with item lines so one concert can cover many instruments and support partial returns; responsible person is stored as name + phone because they may not be a portal user.

nodes.label: checked_out item status
nodes.rationale: A fully-out item shows as checked out and reverts to its previous status when everything is back; a damaged return sets the item condition to what was recorded and flags it.

nodes.label: Check-out wizard flow
nodes.rationale: Four steps - event details, items with available quantity, condition and at least 2 required photos, review and confirm - triggered from the room page row action, an All items bulk action, or a New checkout button. Upload opens the camera on phones because this is mostly done on a phone at the door.

nodes.label: Return wizard flow
nodes.rationale: Supports partial return; shows the original checkout photos alongside the return photos so the receiver can compare before and after on the spot. Status becomes returned when all lines are back, partially_returned otherwise.

nodes.label: Webhook verification flaw (hardcoded Paystack signature)
nodes.rationale: POST /webhooks/{gateway} hardcodes the x-paystack-signature header and assumes isValidSignature() exists, so a tgipay webhook would fatal because TgiPayGateway does not implement it; TGIPAY is instead reconciled through the user redirect callback.

nodes.label: Checkout availability rules
nodes.rationale: Available quantity = item quantity minus quantity out on unreturned lines; over-checkout and lost/under-repair/disposed items are blocked, and checkout and return run in DB transactions with row locks on the items so two people cannot both take the last unit.

nodes.label: Photo evidence trail rule
nodes.rationale: The 2-photos-per-line minimum is validated server-side in the action/service, not just marked required in the form, and once confirmed photos cannot be deleted or replaced by anyone below admin because they are the evidence trail; admin changes are logged.

nodes.label: ceo role (read-only, all branches, costs)
nodes.rationale: CEO needs oversight across every branch including purchase costs, but must not be able to write, so the register cannot be altered from the top.

nodes.label: Inventory Module + Scoped Inventory Officer Role spec
nodes.norm_label: inventory module + scoped inventory officer role spec
nodes.rationale: Goal: a room-by-room asset register across 4 branches maintained by an Inventory Officer who can touch nothing else in the portal, with read-only CEO visibility.

nodes.label: Room grid, room photos and event check-out/return spec
nodes.norm_label: room grid, room photos and event check-out/return spec

nodes.label: Three-layer isolation strategy
nodes.rationale: Navigation hiding alone is not security, so isolation uses three independent layers: a separate Filament panel with its own resource discovery path (no admin route to guess), canAccessPanel() on the User model (403 rather than a redirect loop), and policies plus Spatie permission checks on every resource.

nodes.label: Step 0 - inspect before changing
nodes.rationale: The agent must first summarise existing models, image storage, roles and branch scoping, then propose a migration list and wait for approval; all migrations must be additive, never dropping or renaming columns that hold existing data.

nodes.label: inventory.view_costs permission
nodes.rationale: Withheld from the officer so a field role never sees purchase prices, which is usually what you actually want.

nodes.label: ItemResource (Filament)
nodes.rationale: Defaults to grouping by room.name so the table reads as a room-by-room walkthrough, matching how the officer physically works; cost fields appear only with inventory.view_costs and there is no bulk delete for the officer.

nodes.label: inventory_room.update_photo permission
nodes.rationale: A dedicated "Change photo" action rather than full room edit rights, enforced in the policy and not just by hiding the button, so a branch manager cannot accidentally alter room names or branches or touch another branch's rooms.

nodes.label: Room grid landing view
nodes.rationale: Replaces the collapsible grouped item list with clickable room cards (photo, name, branch, item count, badge for items out at events), responsive 1/2/3-4 columns, staying inside the existing dark Filament theme with amber accent and quiet card chrome.

nodes.label: Inventory room photos
nodes.rationale: Images only, max ~5 MB, resized server-side to ~1600px with a thumbnail conversion for the grid, using whatever image approach the project already uses (a cover single-file collection if Media Library is installed).

nodes.label: Activity-log audit trail
nodes.rationale: Every create/update/delete on inventory_items and inventory_rooms is logged with spatie/laravel-activitylog including acting user and branch, surfaced as a read-only History tab, so when the CEO asks why 6 fans became 4 the answer is one click away.

nodes.label: Permissions deliberately withheld from the officer
nodes.norm_label: permissions deliberately withheld from the officer
nodes.rationale: room.delete, item.delete, item.dispose, inventory.view_costs and category.manage stay with CEO/super admin, because deletion and disposal are how an asset register gets quietly falsified; the officer instead marks an item missing or needs_repair and it surfaces on the CEO exceptions list.

nodes.label: All items flat table
nodes.rationale: A flat Rooms/All items toggle is kept so someone searching for "Yamaha keyboard" does not have to open rooms one by one.

nodes.label: app:send-fee-reminders Artisan command
nodes.rationale: Queries students owing money and queues one delayed SendWhatsAppMessage per debtor; it owns the delay accumulation so the job itself stays stateless.

nodes.label: Evolution API docker-compose deployment
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the fastest secure path onto a Linux server; required env covers the global API token, webhook features and the data store.

nodes.label: Evolution API /message/sendText endpoint
nodes.rationale: Called with Laravel's Http::withToken()->post() facade rather than a custom client, so the token handling and timeouts stay standard.

nodes.label: WhatsApp QR instance pairing via Manager dashboard
nodes.norm_label: whatsapp qr instance pairing via manager dashboard
nodes.rationale: A dedicated WhatsApp Business SIM is paired by QR scan so school traffic never runs through a personal number.

nodes.label: Staff registration alert on new student
nodes.norm_label: staff registration alert on new student

nodes.label: Anti-ban messaging architecture
nodes.rationale: Meta's anti-spam filters ban numbers that blast messages in tight loops, so the design forbids synchronous foreach sends, pushes every message through a queued job, and spaces sends with randomized human-like gaps to keep the unofficial number alive.

nodes.label: Graceful try/catch around the Evolution API call
nodes.norm_label: graceful try/catch around the evolution api call
nodes.rationale: An unofficial API endpoint will go down, time out or return bad statuses; the job logs the failure and returns instead of throwing, so one dead endpoint cannot take the whole queue system with it.

nodes.label: Staggered cumulative randomized delay (5-10s)
nodes.rationale: sleep() inside the job would block the queue worker, so the dispatcher accumulates a random 5-10 second offset per message and passes it to Laravel's ->delay(), giving human-like pacing (0s, 7s, 15s, 21s, ...) without holding a worker hostage.

nodes.rationale: Three ways forward were offered: scan the QR to populate instance numbers (recommended), flip DATABASE_SAVE_DATA_CONTACTS to true and re-run, or import a CSV / query the portal DB directly.

nodes.rationale: Reminder sending needs debtor student data, so a template CSV was generated for the user to fill and an import command is the next agent's task.

nodes.label: Anti-duplicate CSV importer pattern
nodes.rationale: Matches on serial_number first, then branch_code + room_code + name + brand, and reports skipped duplicates rather than failing the whole batch.

nodes.label: Leading quantity parsing ("6 chairs")
nodes.rationale: Source sheets bury quantity in the item text, so the importer splits a leading number into quantity and keeps the remainder as the item name; duplicate asset tags and duplicate items in the same branch/room are skipped rather than failing the batch.

nodes.label: Mobile audit capture page
nodes.rationale: The officer walks rooms with a phone, so the audit page is a stripped custom Livewire page (one item per row, big +/- stepper, sticky save). Saving per line rather than per audit means a dropped connection loses one row, not an hour of counting.

nodes.label: Broken item thumbnail fix
nodes.rationale: Images must be fixed before building anything that depends on them; likely causes are a missing php artisan storage:link, files on a private disk, a wrong APP_URL, or the column rendering a raw path instead of a URL.

nodes.rationale: Sanctum bearer tokens protect the API; its migrations ship with the standard migrate run.

nodes.label: Stateless Mobile API v1
nodes.rationale: A fully stateless, token-based v1 RESTful API in routes/api.php for a companion mobile app; responses are standardized JSON wrapped in API Resources so the mobile client sees a stable contract independent of Eloquent model shape.

nodes.label: Student Management
nodes.rationale: Full lifecycle management from admission to graduation.

nodes.label: API Integration Blueprint Brief
nodes.rationale: An architect-persona prompt asking for a structured blueprint to layer a clean, secure REST API over the existing live Laravel + Filament portal for a mobile counterpart app.

nodes.label: Robots Crawler Policy (Allow All)
nodes.rationale: User-agent: * with an empty Disallow permits all crawlers on every path — the Laravel default, left unrestricted even though the portal serves authenticated student data, since that data sits behind auth rather than behind robots rules.

nodes.label: Tenstrings Portal
nodes.rationale: A comprehensive music school management system built on Laravel 12 and Filament PHP v3, chosen to get admin/instructor/student back-office UI without hand-building CRUD.

nodes.label: Hand-Written Controllers vs Filament REST Plugin
nodes.norm_label: hand-written controllers vs filament rest plugin
nodes.rationale: An explicit open trade-off: write standard Laravel API controllers from scratch (control, clean JSON contract) versus adopting a Filament REST API plugin (speed, coupling to panel resources). The decision was left to be argued with pros and cons for this stack.

nodes.label: Mobile Token Storage and Fetch Pattern
nodes.norm_label: mobile token storage and fetch pattern
nodes.rationale: The mobile frontend (React Native or Swift, left as a choice) must store the bearer token securely rather than in plain storage, and attach it to sample GET requests.

nodes.label: Stateless API vs Stateful Filament Constraint
nodes.norm_label: stateless api vs stateful filament constraint
nodes.rationale: Filament and Livewire rely on stateful session authentication, so the new mobile API must be stateless and its auth setup must coexist with the existing admin panel without breaking it — this is stated as the crucial constraint driving the whole design.

nodes.label: Dynamic Branch Pricing (Luxury Centers)
nodes.rationale: is_luxury_branch and markup_percentage on the Branch model let premium locations (e.g. 20% markup for Ajah) be priced by data rather than duplicated catalogs; the Advanced Diploma series is deliberately exempted because those programs are already priced at a premium and double-marking them would distort the catalog.

nodes.label: API/Filament Guard Separation
nodes.rationale: The token API is strictly separated from the web portal's session-based Filament guards, so adding mobile auth cannot break existing admin panel logins; deployments touching guards require optimize:clear.

nodes.label: Import Duplicate Resolution Cascade
nodes.rationale: Existing students are matched by student_number, then email, then the first_name + last_name + phone triple; matched rows are updated with the latest financial snapshot instead of erroring or creating duplicates, so repeated imports are idempotent.

nodes.label: Unlocked Lesson Progression
nodes.rationale: Lessons unlock progressively; the mobile courses endpoints must respect the same unlock logic as the web portal so the API cannot be used to skip ahead.

nodes.label: Multi-Panel Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separate Filament panels for Admins, Instructors, and Students keep role-specific surfaces and guards isolated rather than gating one shared panel by permission.

nodes.label: Production Deployment Procedure
nodes.rationale: composer install --optimize-autoloader --no-dev, migrate --force, then optimize:clear — the cache clear matters specifically because cached config/routes would otherwise serve stale auth guard definitions after API changes.

nodes.label: UserRoleSeeder Overhashing Fix
nodes.rationale: Hash::make() in the seeder combined with a model-level hashed cast double-hashed admin passwords, silently breaking default admin logins; the fix removes the explicit hash and relies on the cast alone.

nodes.label: InventoryPermissionSeeder
nodes.rationale: Must be re-run on every deploy that changes role permissions, because role-permission state lives in the database rather than in code.

nodes.label: Pending Hostinger deploy tasks
nodes.rationale: Update .env with the new IP and token, git pull origin main, then php artisan queue:restart - the queue worker holds the old config until restarted.

nodes.label: Three-place branch restriction
nodes.rationale: Branch restriction is enforced in three places - model query scope, policies for direct links, and create/import handling - so an officer cannot reach another branch by guessing a URL or by picking another branch in a form or the CSV import dialog.

nodes.label: EVOLUTION_API_URL / EVOLUTION_API_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: The Laravel app on Hostinger reaches the API through these two env vars; the token is the container's AUTHENTICATION_API_KEY.

nodes.label: app:send-fee-reminders command
nodes.rationale: Dispatches the queued job with a cumulative staggered delay so messages go out sequentially rather than in a burst that looks like spam to WhatsApp.

nodes.label: Manager UI QR-scan flow
nodes.rationale: Requires MANAGER_ENABLED=true; if the Manager UI is unreachable, the QR is generated through POST /instance/connect/{instance} and returned as base64.

nodes.label: Port 8080 exposure vs HTTPS reverse proxy
nodes.norm_label: port 8080 exposure vs https reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Hostinger must reach the API over the internet, so either port 8080 is opened in the AWS security group or an Nginx/Caddy + Let's Encrypt reverse proxy fronts it on a subdomain, avoiding a raw unencrypted port.

nodes.label: EC2 t3.small upgrade and redis container
nodes.norm_label: ec2 t3.small upgrade and redis container
nodes.rationale: The instance was upgraded from t3.micro (1GB) to t3.small (2GB) because the internal Baileys engine crashed from lack of memory while generating the QR code, and a redis container was added to docker-compose.yml to stop a continuous crash loop. The upgrade changed the public IP to 16.171.12.145.

nodes.label: /student profile endpoints
nodes.rationale: change-password revokes all tokens on success, so the client must re-authenticate afterwards; documents are returned as signed URLs.

nodes.label: HTTP client interceptors and 401 handling
nodes.rationale: Attach Authorization: Bearer automatically and globally clear the token and redirect to Login on 401; data fetching must account for the Laravel API Resource data wrapper (response.data.data).

nodes.label: Bearer-token-only Sanctum rule
nodes.rationale: The web backend uses Filament with stateful cookie session guards, so the mobile app must use Sanctum bearer tokens only - SPA cookie authentication would conflict with Filament.

nodes.label: Secure token storage directive
nodes.rationale: expo-secure-store on React Native (never AsyncStorage) or Keychain on Swift, because the bearer token is the only credential and AsyncStorage is unencrypted.
